Painting Restoration Report — p026

Extended painting-level restoration evidence, sensitivity experiments, limitations, and review actions

Executive Summary

This report covers all 37 approved cases and 141 approved restoration candidates for p026. It includes 4 experiments, 9 damage families, and 4 evaluated models.

Direct conclusion: LaMa has the better preliminary-review profile because 73.0% of its candidates require manual review. Stable Diffusion has the worse profile at 100.0%. This is a descriptive flag comparison, not an overall restoration-quality ranking. Metric-specific results can identify a better and worse model for one measure, but the painting-wide ordering remains inconclusive. The evidence supports human review rather than automatic acceptance.

Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness.

Recommended review actions

  • Inspect all seeds together; do not select one attractive output without reporting variability.
  • Inspect colour matching inside the restored region.
  • Inspect colour transfer across the mask boundary.
  • Inspect edges and brushwork inside the repair crop.
  • Inspect global layout and unchanged context; seek specialist review when critical.
  • Inspect major contours and spatial layout; seek specialist review when critical.
  • Inspect repeated motifs and generated-looking surface detail.
  • Inspect texture continuity across the repair boundary.
  • Inspect the boundary ring at full resolution.
  • Inspect the repaired region against the clean reference and error map.
More triggered flags mean that a candidate needs stronger human review. They are decision-support signals, not expert conservation labels or automatic rejection decisions.

Limitations

  • The evidence evaluates digital reconstruction, not physical conservation treatment.
  • Repeated candidates and prompt variants are nested within cases and paintings.
  • SDXL has partial coverage and must not be compared as though it covered all cases.
  • Perceptual and feature models are not conservation-specific.
  • A better metric result does not establish historical authenticity.
  • A worse flag profile does not by itself establish unusable visual quality.
  • Overall model selection remains inconclusive when metric families disagree.
